desc: Dun Morogh Links: a SNOW golf course. Keep EXACTLY the layout, landmarks and camera of the FIRST image (the same winding course, frozen lake, dwarven stone clubhouse with its chimney, ram, snowy pines and the carved gate of Ironforge in the mountain) - only the materials change: NO green grass anywhere. The fairway is a groomed strip of smooth packed white snow with faint mower-like stripes, the rough is deep fluffy snow drifts, the putting green is a smooth round sheet of hard-packed glittering snow and ice with the red flag. Crisp blue sky, cold bright light. Paint it in the soft painted style of the other images

The Great Forge Green: a STONE golf course inside the dwarven city of Ironforge. Keep EXACTLY the layout, landmarks and camera of the FIRST image (the great carved dwarf-face pillars, the glowing lava falls and the Great Forge pool as the water hazard, the hanging chains and anvil, the gryphon by the flag) - only the materials change: NO grass and NO plants anywhere. The fairway is worn grey dwarven flagstone paving in big square tiles with gold-inlaid edges, the rough is rubble and broken masonry, the putting green is a smooth polished round slab of dark granite with a brass-rimmed hole and the red flag. Warm orange forge light, embers. Paint it in the soft painted style of the other images

Westfall Links: a golden YELLOW golf course in Westfall: the fairway is mown golden wheat stubble and dry yellow grass, the rough is tall swaying golden wheat fields, the putting green a smooth patch of pale straw-gold turf with the red flag, a creaky wooden windmill and a red Westfall farmhouse barn, a patched scarecrow caddie leaning on a golf bag, a Harvest Golem mowing in the distance, the Westfall lighthouse on the coast far behind, warm hazy late-summer sun, everything in yellows and golds

Redridge Links: a REDDISH golf course in the Redridge Mountains: the fairway is short rust-red grass and red clay, the rough is red rocks and autumn shrubs in reds and oranges, the putting green a smooth patch of deep russet turf with the red flag beside Lake Everstill as the water hazard, red rock cliffs and ridges all around, the wooden bridge and stone houses of Lakeshire across the water, a gnoll peeking from behind a red boulder, warm autumn light, everything in reds, rusts and oranges
